reviews.text: Broken into ten cheeky episodic chapters and boasting beautiful natural beauty, you will find a fun experience that may feel familiar, yet is wholly unique.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Waititi's long-in-development adaptation of the Crump's classic has a style and wit all of its own. Neill is delightfully grumpy, but it is Dennison who steals the show. The over the top buffoonery of the final chase is a bit much, though
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: The balance between humanity and comedy is what Taika Waititi does best.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: This fun little odyssey pulls from so many directions but always maintains its balance. It’s genuinely tender and sweet but never overly sentimental.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Achieves a pitch-perfect balance of silly humor and compassionate characters, proving both oddly funny and profoundly moving despite some very clichéd archetypes propelling the story.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The truly rare family film that's safe for kids, funny and acerbic enough for adults, and surprising enough to keep everyone absorbed.
reviews.author: Toussaint Egan

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is excellent when it focuses solely on the relationship between - and the misadventures of - its two central figures. It's less captivating when the attention turns to several doltish supporting characters.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It's like Rushmore in the bush - yes, it's Bushmore
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: A little bit Rambo, a little bit The Goonies, and as good a time as you can ever hope to have in the cinema.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Bombastic chases, dark humour, and poignantly truthful moments make Hunt For The Wilderpeople more meaningful than many other big name action or comedies out there. Definitely a film that everyone should see.
reviews.author: Heidy Morales

reviews.text: Waititi sneaks some bigger ideas in there behind the chase scenes and the shootouts and the crazy characters...
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: It's mostly effective and funny, though not every moment works entirely.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: It's a unique adventure film that isn't a waste of your time or money.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: The two leads have a fantastic chemistry, both comedic and emotional, and Wilderpeople deftly mixes action, comedy, and drama.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Waititi proves it by maintaining a cartoonish tone that very well balances drama, comedy, and a sentimentality well worth getting excited for. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: ...deliciously deadpan...
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Funny, exciting, and deeply moving, Hunt for the Wilderpeople is unlike anything you've ever seen, even though you've seen plenty of things like it.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: The always funny Rhys Darby makes a third act appearance as Hunt for the Wilderpeople treks deeper into the unrestrained realm of adventure comedy with absurd glee.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: There is a beating heart amidst the crackling one-liners, which once again elevates Waititi's storytelling from the merely entertaining to the instant classic.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: It has everything you want in a film - memorable characters, an interesting story, and, most importantly, heart.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: The director assures to reinforce the universality of what he wants to tell over stereotypes. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: A droll walk in the woods.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: You saw growth but it felt natural and believable instead of cornball material it could have been.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: THE HUNT FOR THE WILDERPEOPLE possesses a cheerful brand of comedy that is as charming as it is inventive, and it's complemented by great scenes of emotion that ring true throughout its soul-searching adventure.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Both Ricky and Hec are dealing with grief and their journey is a sentimental mixture of charm, improbable fantasy and farce, with a nod to Thelma and Louise.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Both hilarious and heart felt.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople masks its earnest sweetness with a giggling distrust of authority, making it at once heartfelt and mischievous.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: Too smart by half, and calibrated to within an inch of its life with its wannabe eccentric narrative, gags and 'cool' soundtrack choices.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Julian Dennison is a revelation as the young miscreant forced to team up with a very curmudgeonly Sam Neill as they try to survive in the wilds of New Zealand.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: This warmed my heart plenty on the cold night that I watched it, and that's exactly what I needed.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Hector and Ricky build an uneasy and finally heartwarming camaraderie.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople transforms a fairly unremarkable tale of adoption into a wild and wonderful fantasy, yet again proving that New Zealand may as well just be Middle Earth.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: It's just so sophisticated and mordantly humorous you don't notice at first that it's also in the tradition of a classic boy's adventure tale.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: a leisurely and hopeful coming-of-age comedy adapted from Barry Crump's 1986 novel, Wild Pork and Watercress.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: It all sounds very serious, but it's not at all, with director Taika Waititi injecting a rich vein of dark humour and a cast of eccentric characters to deliver something that is weird, funny and mildly moving.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: ... Wilderpeople isn't just charming or good-it's a legitimately great film.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: It's funny, sweet, sad, and exhilarating all at once.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Wilderpeople is a hugely loveable movie that's suitable for date night or the whole family, and I know that sounds like a hacky movie poster blurb. But when a movie's this good, it's tough to avoid clichs.
reviews.author: Ned Lannamann

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople tackles some fairly serious issues, but it handles those issues with just the right sense of the sweet.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: It has all the makings of a new childhood classic: it's got wonder and adventure and loads of humor, and ultimately winds up on the side of optimism - but it also has moments of genuine tragedy and danger.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: A film about romanticism, respect, acceptance and loyalty, however, it becomes excellent because of the construction of one of the most wonderful characters that modern cinema has given us. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: Its whackiness and borderline fantasy might not be for everyone, but there's a universal, childlike appeal to the story that feels too powerful to deny.
reviews.author: Alex Casey

reviews.text: I can't remember the last time I laughed this much at a movie. This wacky adventure set in New Zealand's wilderness is outrageously funny. It is filled with quirky, compelling characters and witty dialog.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Wilderpeople emerges as a hugely likeable but not always coherent yarn.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: While there are numerous nods to cultural references only a local audience will appreciate, Ricky and Hec's emotional journey is one which every viewer can climb aboard.
reviews.author: Sarah Watt

reviews.text: Gentle and appealing performances can't rescue this facile and cloying comedy.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: [Its] sheer good-naturedness pulls off a not particularly inspired crusty-old-coot-thawed-by-young-scamp concept, maintaining an agreeable tonal balance despite occasional wobbles between spoof, sentimentality and silliness.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: In Hunt for the Wilderpeople by Taika Waititi, lush landscapes of the rainforest of New Zealand counter a sense of humor so toast-dry that it makes the British Ealing comedies of the 1950s seem overripe.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: The film would be thuddingly familiar if not for Waititi's willingness to grasp overused tropes and manipulate them into something new.
reviews.author: Chris Plante

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is one of the most entertaining films of the year.
reviews.author: Cassam Looch

reviews.text: Warmly funny and deeply delightful.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is very likely the summer's most magical film.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: This is really a wonderful adventure-comedy.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: One of the most sincere and funny portraits of family life to come along in a while.
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: Sweeping cinematography (by Lachlan Milne) and playful editing (by Luke Haigh, Tom Eagles and Yana Gorskaya) make the adventure all the more majestical.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: Strictly for those who love pie-eyed problem pics with scenic wanderlust.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: What keeps all this enchantment grounded is the characters.
reviews.author: Jennifer Panzera

reviews.text: It's formulaic at heart, but has a sweet, unpredictable sense of humour and a nice way with words.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople might just be Waititi's most triumphant moment to date.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: A splendidly morbid comedy for the whole family.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is unabashedly sentimental, and some of the specific tragic notes threaten to come across as cloying, but the comedy gives it a lot of life.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wang

reviews.text: Waititi shows a larger scope than his previous films, with overhead shots surveying the gorgeous New Zealand landscape. A snowy montage scene set to Leonard Cohen recalls Robert Altman's 1971 opus McCabe and Mrs. Miller.
reviews.author: Jimmy Geurts

reviews.text: In the hands director Taika Waititi, who mixes sentimentality with spiky, even absurdist humor, it's a remarkable treat.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: [The film] has a laidback, gentle tone - one that makes the viewer lean in to listen carefully.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: ...looks as funny as it sounds.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: ... a coming of age comedy with a heartwarming soul that never slips into easy sentiment.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: This film is an adventure itself, a gem that surely will become brighter over time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: A mixture of comedy, drama, whimsy and anarchy (and with plenty of charm to spare, even if sometimes the tone wavers a little), this is almost impossible not to like, and it's the strong characters that draw you in.
reviews.author: James Bartlett

reviews.text: There's brilliant chemistry between Dennison and Neil, the pair quite obviously bouncing off each other; a joy to watch on screen, and as the story progresses you begin to feel like a member of their special pack, gleefully part of the adventure.
reviews.author: Jack Shepherd

reviews.text: The film's main asset is an unaffected naturalism, both in the film-making, and in the unpolished characters that we root for.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople has been a huge audience favourite at festivals this year and you can see why, with its brand of dark New Zealand humour, coupled with a boy's own adventure story that goes not merely off the rails, but off-road and off-grid.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: It's hard to imagine anybody not being won over by this charming adventure, which I'm already looking forward to watching again.
reviews.author: Martin Roberts

reviews.text: This charming comedy combines endearing characters with generous helpings of deadpan humour - and the result is quite wonderful.
reviews.author: Stephen Carty

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a fun, funny family yarn.
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: A sweet crowdpleaser guaranteed to lift your spirits.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: It's far from original - grumpy-old-git-bond-with-mouthy-adolescent - but is delivered with such joy-infused enthusiasm it's almost impossible to resist.
reviews.author: Tim Evans

reviews.text: It's a not unpromising set-up -- masculinity left to fend for itself against Mother Nature -- and I wished Waititi had made merry with his hapless hunter-gatherers in the same way Shadows did with wannabe outlaw vampires.
reviews.author: Mike McCahill

reviews.text: Waititi keeps the jokes coming thick and fast, delivering hi-jinks and heightened characters with an emotional undertow that really resonates.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Without actively disliking any part of it, you wish you could be on your way a whole hour before it limps to a close.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: An inward-looking comedy that's not afraid to poke fun at its country's own foibles but still manages to feel like a celebration of life on a little island.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: Growing up, growing old and the grief that's part of both is beautifully handled here with a quirky mix of humour and heart.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Warm, witty, and occasionally wild, Waititi's bush-bonding romp is a kind, generous-spirited winner.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: This might be the best kids' movie since Up.
reviews.author: Tom Huddleston

reviews.text: Delightful... Ends up being sweet and affecting despite its characters' disdain for mushy stuff.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: A bit Up, a bit Moonrise Kingdom, a bit Midnight Run, even... Taika Waititi's latest is an oddball treat of a mismatched-buddy pursuit move.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: While I could go on and on about what good company Neill and Dennison are, it's an actress named Rima Te Wiata who works the most magic.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Bring a hanky.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: It's a classic reluctant camaraderie story with emotion that sways like trees in a gentle breeze between sad, bittersweet, and rambunctious adventure.
reviews.author: Neil Miller

reviews.text: Neill could play a cranky old bushman in his sleep, but it's Julian Dennison as Ricky who steals the film as a rap-loving, pre-pubescent gangster wannabe. This kid's a find.
reviews.author: Austin Trunick

reviews.text: ... uses familiar themes to launch a exploration of misfit male bonding and surrogate families with heartfelt tenderness and visual flair.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This charming, witty and heartfelt film about the meaning of family might just remind you that there really are fresh voices at the movies.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: The byplay between the newcomer Dennison and the veteran Neill is delightful, as the two characters' faades slowly melt and a genuine bond of affection develops.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a refreshing alternative to standard Hollywood children's fare.
reviews.author: T'Cha Dunlevy

reviews.text: "Wilderpeople" isn't Taititi's best work, but it's impressively executed, making time for broad antics and intimate exchanges without unraveling into a mess of ideas.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Waititi's most iconically "New Zealand" movie shows a deep love of the country's "majestical" landscapes and the rough-and-tumble people that live in its hidden places.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It has too many strained feel-good moments for my comfort zone.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Yet another home run from Taika Waititi...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople treads on such familiar ground that it's a miracle it works as well as it does.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Waititi's film has the stylized exaggerations and emotional directness of the best children's literature. Everything is just a tiny bit louder and more colorful than real life, but the feelings are straightforward and unadorned.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople shows us a cruel, unsentimental and thankless world, and yet we're made to love that world anyway.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: This is a movie you watch with minor pleasure when you happen upon it channel surfing on cable TV. Leaving home for it and selecting it over and above a city's full cinematic outlay is another matter.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: Flawed 'Wilderpeople' has its requisite charms.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: When this film earns your tears... and it will... it does it honestly, and I suspect this is a film that people are going to share by word of mouth for years, one of those rare gems that will play equally well for viewers of any age.
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: Great screen chemistry and shimmering cinematography make this film work.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: Few films have ever been less likely to get but more deserving of a sequel.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Its heartwarming message combined with creative, fantastical elements make it unique and memorable.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The story, told in Wes Anderson-style storybook chapters with titles like "Goodbye Ricky Baker" and "Close to the Sky," grows ever more absurd, almost to the breaking point.
reviews.author: Joanna Connors

reviews.text: "Wilderpeople" is one of those rare movies that works for almost any generation, silly and sweet and big-hearted. To quote Hec, it's a majestical piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" is a hoot with heart.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: A 60 year-old man and a 12-year old boy's walk on the wild side in New Zealand.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Director Taika Waititi proves expert in his management of tone, such that the farcical elements, however numerous, don't detract from the very real friendship the renegades develop as they elude the world's most dedicated social services officer.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a thoughtful and hilarious film with nuanced performances from the two leads.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: A charming coming-of-age film set in the New Zealand bush, complete with a company of quirky, mismatched characters.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: A warm-hearted, funny, well-crafted coming-of-age story.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: ... Hunt for the Wilderpeople is a wonderfully executed genre cocktail where one moment will leave you breathless from laughter, the next recovering from heartache.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Has more genuinely funny moments than most so-called comedies at the multiplex, abetted by Waititi's now-practiced comic sensibility, his stylized snap of performance and editing.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is all about life-changing moments and the people who are the catalysts. It's about learning from those around you, regardless of age or circumstance.
reviews.author: Miriam Di Nunzio

reviews.text: It takes a well-worn premise and turns it into a quirkily funny delight.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: HUNT FOR THE WILDERPEOPLE, the most endearing buddy comedy adventure you'll see this year. It has all the wit and its crafty humor will keep you laughing and entertained from beginning to end. See this movie as soon as you can.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: There is so much goodness, such an unabashed sense of decency, in the first act of Hunt for the Wilderpeople that the sentiment carries through the rest of the film...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's a beautiful and moving "buddy" story --- full of hilarity.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Without the exceptional performances from Sam Neill and Julian Dennison, "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" would likely devolve into an outlandish situation comedy-wannabe.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Given Waititi's creativity, I was a little disappointed in how few surprises there are in Wilderpeople. But it's all right to be just a well-executed charmer -- and this movie is certainly that.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Quirky Kiwi dramedy promotes teamwork, friendship.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: A lopsided gem full of off-kilter humor, hard truths and real emotion. Great for preteens and up.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Waititi looks for humor in quirks of character and degrees of stubbornness, and the natural challenges of Crump's wilderness journey generate a succession of belly laughs onscreen as the gruff old man scraps with the loudmouthed kid.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Laugh-out-loud funny one minute, achingly sad the next, "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" takes the audience on a rollicking yet poignant journey through the New Zealand backcountry in the company of a pair of engagingly eccentric characters.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: A kind and moving story bristling with honest humor and genuine affection for its characters.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Dennison is a marvel, completely unself-conscious in his portrayal of a kid who is lost but thinks if he acts tough, it'll look like he's found. Neill, playing a different sort of character for him (quiet, unfriendly), is also outstanding.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The movie's intense charm, killer performances, and offbeat music -- from Nina Simone to '70s soft rock -- make it a must-see for 2016.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" has much to recommend it, but none of it would work unless Hec and Ricky are believable and have chemistry. Fortunately, they do.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: The cranky charisma of the performers, plus the cheerfully idiosyncratic rhythms of Waititi's filmmaking, keep it clicking.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: As funny as it is scary. But it's also utterly charming, and surprisingly moving in ways you'd never expect.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople manages to be touching without turning sappy, and funny without relying on cheap humor.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople magically taps into the logic, thought processes, and emotions of a child. It's a rich, strange, and wondrous world.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: Hunt For the Wilderpeople is funny, moving, enthralling and exciting, and impossible to not be drawn into.
reviews.author: Andrew Marshall

reviews.text: May sound like a National Geographic special but is actually a genuine, offbeat road trip comedy/coming-of-age film.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A New Zealand import with a knack for finding humor in dreary, even ill-advised themes.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: Waititi is an expansive, warm-hearted humanist. The fun he pokes is strictly superficial, never grazing his characters' vital organs or essential dignity.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: One of the year's most transportive comedies.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: Like What We Do In The Shadows, Wilderpeople is laugh-out-loud funny and full of left-turn surprises.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: Full of off-kilter characters, an improbable set of events, and a touching if predictable ending, Hunt for the Wilderpeople is as enjoyable to watch as it is a gorgeously shot film.
reviews.author: Josh Lasser

reviews.text: Neill and Dennison's chemistry ensures this unusual survival story is so knee-deep in charm that even moments of gloopy pathos feel thoroughly earned.
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: An oddball and oddly affecting take on two misfits finding their metaphorical partner-in-crime match.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Hunt for the Wilderpeople is ultimately disarming in its innocent sincerity.
reviews.author: Kenji Fujishima

reviews.text: a hilarious and heartfelt adventure that's a Kiwi twist on the curmudgeonly Carl and overweight outsider Russell of Pixar's "Up" by way of the outlaws that were "Thelma and Louise."
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: New Zealand writer-director Taika Waititi blends sharply cynical humour with huge heart in arguably his best film to date, Hunt for the Wilderpeople.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" is consistently clever and even moving. It's proof that we'll keep listening to the familiar stories if they're this well-told.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Wilderpeople is fully redeemed by its sense of humor, both deadpan and broad, well-delivered through the strong performances.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: 101 minutes of pure comic joy.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Waititi's films have a lively energy that provides a delicious counterpoint to the understated comedy.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Wilderpeople is ultimately winning, like all buddy comedies, because of the chemistry of its leads.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" takes a troika of familiar story types - the plucky kid, the crusty geezer, the nurturing bosom - and strips them of clich.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Ricky is a wonderfully fresh creation, the embodiment of hilarity because he doesn't see anything funny about anything, least of all himself.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: A familiar sort of coming-of-age movie made more interesting by the uniqueness of its setting and its off-kilter Kiwi humor.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: Every once in a while, a small, unheralded film comes along, so smart and funny, such a pleasure to experience, you can't believe your luck. "Hunt for the Wilderpeople" is such a film.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: We know we're in good hands from the opening moments, when the New Zealand greenery undulates across the screen while an otherworldly choral chant fills the soundtrack.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: Enjoy this wonderfully unpredictable, eccentric tale.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It's off-beat in all the best ways, has fantastic actors all delivering fantastic performances, and is a uproarious adventure with endless heart.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Dennison juggles foulmouthed brattiness and sweet sincerity well enough, and Neill soars as a gruff outdoorsman hiding a soft, chewy center.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: A delightful little movie that ranks as one of the more pleasant surprises of the year thus far.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: An enjoyably goofy adventure that manages to bring some freshness to the moldy "cantankerous adult reluctantly bonds with adorable kid" subgenre.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: [A] lovely little study of bonding and healing in the New Zealand bush.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: In the midst of another big blockbuster summer, this raffish comedy-adventure provides a breath of fresh air.
reviews.author: Michael Sauter

reviews.text: It infuses an outdoorsy survival tale and a coming-of-age story of friendship with Taika Waititi's penchant for distaff flakiness.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: A wonderful slice of New Zealand-bred humor that should have a far wider appeal than Waititi's previous films.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: A rollicking, joke-filled, brightly-colored boys' adventure where both boy and adult get to be boys.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: As a transient feel-good movie it certainly is 'magestical'.
reviews.author: Matthew Anderson

reviews.text: Quirky outsider comedy is clearly Waititi's forte, and here it's polished to an effortlessly funny, confident and crowd-pleasing shine.
reviews.author: Michelle Devereaux

reviews.text: A deliciously good time at the movies.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: This is Waititi's best film yet. The way he mixes tones throughout the film is a thing of beauty.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: With its youthful protagonist, wicked sense of humor, and monstrous depiction of authority figures, the spirit of Roald Dahl is alive and well in Hunt for the Wilderpeople.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Offbeat, intimate and impressively affecting, this Kiwi comedy is one of the year's strongest films to date.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: This may sound like a standard adventure narrative or buddy film, but Waititi magnificently feels out the nuances with enormous heart.
reviews.author: Lachlan Kanoniuk

reviews.text: It's quite possibly the best movie (so far) this year.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: New Zealand has never looked more breath-taking (and fearsome) and the performances are all tremendous here.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Dennison holds his own opposite Neill, who hasn't been tasked with such a gravely amusing role in years. Together, the two are comic dynamite.
reviews.author: Nigel M. Smith

reviews.text: It's like being killed with kindness, a good problem to have but a hard one to define beyond pleasantries
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: Waititi, who wrote the screenplay based on a novel by Barry Crump, is pretty fearless in his tonal palette ... It's not your conventional, conservative kid's flick, to its definite credit.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Sam Neill is as good as he's ever been, spurred on by his unpredictable and lively offsider, Julian Dennison. It's a good sign when you don't want a movie to end.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: [An] immensely likable film.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: This film is a rough-cut, homegrown gem.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: This deceptively quaint feel-good comedy-adventure instantly finds an arresting storytelling groove that cannot help but win you over. It is, without doubt, one of the best films that will be released in 2016.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: If you're after a film that's funny and sweet and harks back to a certain kind of innocent (but not toothless) 80s action-adventure, then Hunt for the Wilderpeople is perfect.
reviews.author: Rochelle Siemienowicz

reviews.text: ...a very winning comedy.
reviews.author: Julian Wood

reviews.text: In an age of branded films, it's such a relief to stumble upon a film like Hunt for the Wilderpeople. Filmmaking this fresh, this vibrant, and this affecting for all ages is rare these days.
reviews.author: Michael Roffman

reviews.text: The humour here is derived from the gap between a fantastic scenario and the everyday outcomes. It's [Waititi's] ability to create a self-contained world - complete with amateurish songs - which makes the resulting dialogue so amusing.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: I do find New Zealand films refreshingly offbeat, crazy in the most entertaining way, and peopled with characters who inhabit the outer edges of society. In this film, those characteristics are in abundance
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: It's a small film with a big heart and one whose charm resonates and grows on you
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: The Revenant had a lot of things (too many things, even), but it didn't have the heart, humour and hoodies of Taika Waititi's Hunt for the Wilderpeople... one of 2016's best, warmest and wildest comedies.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Wilderpeople is the best film of 2016, so far; or as Ricky and Uncle Hect would say - "sh*t just got real."
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Here is the perfect example of a film that at a glance appears to be going one way, but winds up somewhere far more entertaining and endearing that you could possibly expect.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: It's a gentle movie, but with a bittersweet edge - and it's funny as hell to boot.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Full of character and comedy, it's easily one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Hunt For The Wilderpeople is a comical, soul-searching tale from the Bush that delights around every leaf-covered turn.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: It finds humor and love in a potentially grim situation without ever belittling or caricaturing the characters.
reviews.author: Elise Nakhnikian

reviews.text: Neil proves compellingly gruff as a reluctant father figure, though it's the trash-talking, family-craving ten-year-old Dennison who steals the show, exuding a wacko, wounded attitude rooted in Ricky's backwoods Rambo-Scarface-Mad Max reveries.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The remarkable performance of young Julian Dennison as Ricky Baker, the city juvenile delinquent fostered out in the backblocks, gives Wilderpeople most of its many laughs. But he's not just there doing cute stuff and being precocious.
reviews.author: Russell Baillie

reviews.text: A hilarious, heartwarming tale that harnesses script, direction and performances and takes plenty of creative risks on its way to delivering movie magic.
reviews.author: Steve Newall

reviews.text: A throwback family classic in the mold of The Goonies.
reviews.author: Michael Agresta

reviews.text: While the plot and some of the characters may be a bit cartoonish, the emotions always feel honest and Waititi is able to get some big laughs thanks to his charming protagonists.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: If one imagines a real-life version of Up with a bit of Thelma & Louise thrown in, they get [this] charming on-the-run adventure comedy.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: There's no point where Hunt for the Wilderpeople does anything that you've never seen before, but it would be crazy to hold that against a film made with such an effortlessly cultivated tone and an accommodating ear for comedy.
reviews.author: Russ Fischer

reviews.text: Taika Waititi knows growing up isn't child's play but he also respects childhood as a place of adventure, where spontaneity rules and the possibilities are only limited by imagination.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Built on formula, but when a formula is this well-executed, it's awfully hard to complain.
reviews.author: Scott Renshaw

reviews.text: "Hunt For The Wilderpeople" is a perfectly amicable dramedy that makes a concerted effort to avoid offending or provoking.
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: Waititi manages the balance of tones perfectly and his eye for editing and action show both scale and restraint, so he won't fall short and won't go overboard.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: There aren't a lot of truly fantastic kids movies out there nowadays, but this is one of them.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: A sweetly-told, laugh-out-loud adventure that reminds us you're never too young or too old to find someone to love who'll also love you back.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

synopsis: A boy (Julian Dennison) and his foster father (Sam Neill) become the subjects of a manhunt after they get stranded in the New Zealand wilderness.
